title: Set up the .NET project
summary: Install the .NET 10 SDK, open the Reading List project and build it. Learn what the project files do before connecting Oracle.
introduction: We need a tool that can turn C# files into a running app. That tool comes in the .NET SDK. SDK means software development kit. Think of it as a box of tools for building your program.
learningObjectives: Check that a .NET SDK is installed
Restore packages and build the sample project
Find the controller, model and data files

blocks.text: Install the **.NET 10 SDK**, the long-term support version used here. The runtime alone is not enough to build code. Use the [official .NET download page](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0). Pick the installer for your operating system and processor.
On Windows, you can use this command if the Windows package manager is available. Then open a new terminal so it can find dotnet.

blocks.title: Windows: install and check the SDK

blocks.text: The list should include a 10.0 SDK. A newer compatible SDK can also build the sample because its project file targets net10.0. This course uses .NET 10 features; it does not require .NET 11.

items: Download and extract the ZIP from the first lesson.
Open the extracted dotnet-oracle-backend folder in a code editor.
Open a terminal in that folder. Keep it there for the first command below.

blocks.code:
cd ReadingListApi
dotnet restore
dotnet build
blocks.title: Restore and build the API

blocks.text: **Restore** gets the packages named in ReadingListApi.csproj. **Build** checks the code and creates a runnable program. A successful build does not prove that Oracle is connected. We will test that later.

rows: Chooses net10.0 and names the packages.
Connects the parts and starts the API.
Describes a book and the data a user may send.
Reads and changes rows in Oracle.
Contain setup SQL, useful commands and the optional web page.
blocks.caption: A map of the download

blocks.text: The Oracle driver is called Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core. Version 23.26.400 supports .NET 10. The project pins its package versions so everyone starts with the same code.

blocks.title: Keep the project together
blocks.text: Open the extracted folder, not a file still inside the ZIP. Do not copy bin or obj folders into the tutorial website. They are build output, not lesson content.
Open BooksController.cs and BookRepository.cs. You do not need to understand every line yet. Find the words HttpGet in the first file and SELECT in the second.
